requirements.data_requirements: Storage for user accounts, problem data, code submissions, and performance metrics.

tasks.description: Create the frontend interface for browsing and searching problems in the repository.

tasks.name: Implement Problem Repository Backend
tasks.description: Develop the backend API to manage and serve problem data.

tasks.name: Set Up Problem Database
tasks.description: Design and implement the database schema for storing problem details.

tasks.name: Develop Code Editor UI
tasks.description: Create a frontend code editor with syntax highlighting and basic features.

tasks.name: Integrate Code Editor with Backend
tasks.description: Connect the code editor to the backend for code submission and execution.

tasks.name: Build Online Judge System
tasks.description: Develop the core system to compile and execute user-submitted code and return results.

tasks.name: Test Online Judge System
tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure the online judge system works correctly with various inputs.

tasks.name: Create User Profile UI
tasks.description: Design the frontend interface for user profiles, including user details and activity.

tasks.name: Implement User Profile Backend
tasks.description: Develop the backend API to manage user profile data and activity.

tasks.name: Design Leaderboard UI
tasks.description: Create the frontend interface for displaying the leaderboard with rankings.

tasks.name: Implement Leaderboard Backend
tasks.description: Develop the backend API to calculate and serve leaderboard rankings.

tasks.name: Deploy Application
tasks.description: Deploy the entire application to a production environment.

tasks.name: Perform End-to-End Testing
tasks.description: Test the entire application to ensure all features work as expected.

T1.implementation_approach: Use a component-based approach to design a responsive and user-friendly interface for browsing, searching, and filtering problems.
T1.notes: Focus on intuitive navigation and accessibility.

T2.implementation_approach: Develop RESTful APIs to handle CRUD operations for problems, including endpoints for creating, reading, updating, and deleting problems.
T2.notes: Ensure proper validation and error handling.

T3.implementation_approach: Design a schema to store problem details such as title, description, difficulty, tags, and test cases.
T3.notes: Optimize schema for query performance and scalability.

T4.implementation_approach: Create a code editor interface with syntax highlighting, auto-completion, and error detection.
T4.notes: Ensure compatibility with multiple programming languages.

T5.implementation_approach: Establish WebSocket or REST API communication between the code editor and backend for code execution and result retrieval.
T5.notes: Handle real-time updates and error messages effectively.

T6.implementation_approach: Develop a system to compile and execute code securely in isolated environments, and return results.
T6.notes: Ensure sandboxing and prevent malicious code execution.

T7.implementation_approach: Write unit, integration, and stress tests to validate the functionality and performance of the online judge system.
T7.notes: Simulate edge cases and high-concurrency scenarios.

T8.implementation_approach: Design a user profile page to display user details, activity history, and achievements.

T9.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage user profiles, including endpoints for retrieving and updating user information.
T9.notes: Ensure secure handling of sensitive user data.

T10.implementation_approach: Create a leaderboard interface to display top users based on performance metrics.

T11.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to calculate and retrieve leaderboard data based on user performance metrics.

T12.implementation_approach: Deploy the application using a cloud platform with CI/CD pipelines for automated deployment.
T12.notes: Ensure scalability and monitor application performance.

T13.implementation_approach: Perform end-to-end testing to validate the entire application workflow, from user interaction to backend processing.
T13.notes: Test across multiple devices and browsers.

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

# Initialize SQLAlchemy instance
db = SQLAlchemy()

def init_db(app):
    """
    Initialize the SQLAlchemy database with the given Flask application.

    Args:
        app (Flask): The Flask application instance.
    """
    db.init_app(app)
    with app.app_context():
        db.create_all()

from app.database import db

class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    tags = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=True)  # Comma-separated tags
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Problem id={self.id} title={self.title}>"

from app.database import db

class User(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'users'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(80), unique=True, nullable=False)
    email = db.Column(db.String(120), unique=True, nullable=False)
    password_hash = db.Column(db.String(128), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<User {self.username}>'

from app.database import db

class Solution(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'solutions'
    
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('users.id'), nullable=False)
    problem_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('problems.id'), nullable=False)
    code = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    language = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    status = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)  # e.g., 'Pending', 'Accepted', 'Rejected'
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, server_default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, server_default=db.func.now(), server_onupdate=db.func.now())

    user = db.relationship('User', backref=db.backref('solutions', lazy=True))
    problem = db.relationship('Problem', backref=db.backref('solutions', lazy=True))

# app/routes.py

from app.controllers.problem_controller import problem_blueprint
from app.controllers.user_controller import user_blueprint
from app.controllers.solution_controller import solution_blueprint

def register_blueprints(app):
    """
    Aggregates all blueprints and registers them to the Flask app.
    """
    app.register_blueprint(problem_blueprint, url_prefix='/problems')
    app.register_blueprint(user_blueprint, url_prefix='/users')
    app.register_blueprint(solution_blueprint, url_prefix='/solutions')

__all__ = ['register_blueprints']

from flask import Flask
from app.routes import problem_blueprint, user_blueprint, solution_blueprint
from app.database import db

def create_app():
    app = Flask(__name__)

    # Register blueprints for routing
    app.register_blueprint(problem_blueprint)
    app.register_blueprint(user_blueprint)
    app.register_blueprint(solution_blueprint)

    # Initialize the database
    db.init_app(app)

    return app

from app import create_app

# Entry point for the ACM Problem-Solving Platform application
if __name__ == "__main__":
    app = create_app()
    app.run(host="0.0.0.0", port=5000, debug=True)

# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A web application designed to help users practice and solve ACM-style competitive programming problems.

## Features

- Problem Repository: A comprehensive library of ACM-style problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Editor: An integrated code editor with support for multiple programming languages and syntax highlighting.
- Online Judge System: An automated system to evaluate code submissions and provide real-time feedback on correctness and performance.
- User Profiles: Personalized user accounts to track progress, view solved problems, and analyze performance.
- Leaderboard: A ranking system to compare user performance and encourage competition.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
